newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian minister comments on real estate shares.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian minister comments on real estate shares.

text.p: The Egyptian minister in charge of privatisation said in an interview published on Wednesday that shares in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development might have risen beyond the value justified by its holdings of land.

Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid told the weekly magazine al-Mussawar he thought the share price had risen because large investors were accumulating shares in the hope that land prices would rise in the future.
Capital Market Authority (CMA) Chairman Abdel-Hamid Ibrahim made similar comments about the price of real estate company shares last week but Cairo brokers disputed his analysis.
Medinet Nasr shares, sold by the state at 65.00 pounds ($19) in a landmark privatisation last May, were trading around record levels of 520 pounds a share on Wednesday.
Obeid said Medinet Nasr owned 1,000 acres (400 hectares) of empty land with no utilities connected.
It would cost between 260 and 350 pounds a square metre to install utilities while new communities in the same area offer land with services for 250 to 300 pounds a square metre.
"This means that the land owned by Medinet Nasr did not have the high value which would justify the share price rising in the present way," Obeid said.
"But I do think that the increase is due to the fact that the groups which bought shares in the company are accumulating shares, in the hope that land prices will go up in seven years.
"This may happen or it may not. Land prices could go down as the supply increases," he added.
Ibrahim said investors had driven up the price of real estate shares in the belief that the companies could make quick profits from their land holdings.

"People have been rushing to buy shares in such companies because they expect the value of the land they own will increase greatly and the companies will make big profits from the difference between the book value and the market value.

"What they don't realise is that this land is just a commodity which cannot be sold in a year, for example. This might take years. This has made the shares in the real estate companies rise more than necessary," he said.
Brokers said they continued to believe that Medinet Nasr had a net asset value of about two billion pounds, against a market capitalisation of 1.8 billion pounds at the end of last week.
The brokers said Ibrahim's comments had worried foreign investors but the dispute does not seem to have had much affect on the domestic market for the shares.
The shares rose on Tuesday when investors realised they could still buy shares and be eligible for a free share if they hold on to them until the end of March.
